faculty_override_note: The official two-year, four-semester map is the default. The official five-semester map is an alternate lighter-load pathway. DegreeWorks and faculty advisement remain authoritative. This plan assumes the HIS 101/HIS 102 sequence pair by default; a student pursuing the HIS 115/HIS 116 or HIS 120/HIS 125 pair should adjust the plan with an advisor (see sequence_notes).
sequence_notes: KNOWN LIMITATION: the required History Sequence is 'choose one pair from HIS 101 & HIS 102, or HIS 115 & HIS 116, or HIS 120 & HIS 125.' The current course-selection schema only supports flat choice pools (pick any N courses from a list) and cannot express a linked two-course bundle with mutual exclusivity between bundles. All 6 sequence courses are listed as a single 6-credit requirement; the system does not prevent a student from marking courses from two different pairs (for example HIS 101 and HIS 116) as complete, which would not satisfy the real degree requirement. HIS 102, HIS 116, and HIS 125 each require their own pair's first course as a prerequisite (HIS 101, HIS 115, HIS 120 respectively) as a partial safeguard, but this does not block mixing across pairs. This is flagged for maintainer review; correctly enforcing it would require a schema change beyond this curriculum-data submission.

HIS 275 (History Research and Writing Methods) officially requires ENG 201 plus a completed sequence pair: (HIS 101 and HIS 102) or (HIS 115 and HIS 116) or (HIS 120 and HIS 125). The prerequisite grammar only supports flat AND/OR chains, not grouped '(A and B) or (C and D)' logic, so only the ENG 201 portion is encoded as a course prerequisite; the sequence-completion portion is not enforced.

The non-Western History elective requirement ('at least one course must be a non-western History course') is not mechanically enforced. Courses whose titles clearly indicate non-Western/global regional content are labeled '(non-Western)' in the curriculum data as an advisory aid, based on a good-faith reading of course titles rather than an official BMCC-published non-Western course list. This labeling and the underlying requirement are flagged for maintainer review.
PHI 100 is the shown Individual and Society course; ECO 100 is listed as its alternate.
Select any Creative Expression Pathways course other than SPE 100 or SPE 102 for the second Creative Expression requirement.
Students are advised (not required) to complete 1 course from AFN/HIS 123, AFN/HIS 124, ASN 114, HED 195, HIS 120, HIS 125, or POL 100 for U.S. Experience in Its Diversity.
Students are strongly encouraged (not required) to take a modern language course to satisfy World Cultures and Global Issues.
SPE 102 is the listed alternate to SPE 100 for non-native speakers of English.

A total of 6 credits (2 courses) from AFL, AFN, ANT, ASN, ECO, GEO, HIS, LAT, PHI, POL, PSY, or SOC is required for the Social Science or Ethnic Studies elective; an Ethnic Studies course is an explicit alternate option.
A total of 6 credits (2 courses) of General Elective is required; a 300-level English course, a Health Education course, and/or Modern Language course(s) are recommended but not required.
A Writing Intensive course is required for graduation.
